Two related repos:
- andesim: /home/nick/work/andesim (branch andesim). Hybrid RISC-V simulator orchestration: C++ driver (driver/, ./andesim), QEMU TCG plugin (qemu_plugin/), runtime (runtime/), test harness (tests/, scripts/), docs.
- vsim: /home/nick/work/vsim_andesim. External vsim (SystemC+Verilator) with hybrid orchestration in src/hybrid/*.hpp, cmake/, tests/.

Known history (ground truth for what "legacy" means here — read CLAUDE.md at /home/nick/work/andesim/CLAUDE.md and git log for detail):
- The QEMU2 handback leg was REMOVED: flow is now QEMU1 -> vsim, done. Any code/option/doc still implementing or describing a QEMU2 resume/ship-back step is legacy.
- vsim used to live in-tree under verilator/ in andesim; it moved to the external repo. Anything in andesim still referencing an in-tree verilator/ path, or building vsim locally, is legacy. NOTE: andesim/CLAUDE.md itself has a stale "vsim CMake Structure" section claiming "vsim lives entirely in verilator/" — stale docs count as findings.
- QEMU also moved to an external prebuilt (QEMU_BIN_DIR); anything cloning/building QEMU in-tree is legacy.
- Semihosting/libgloss_vh: nothing in-tree links -lgloss_vh anymore; the vplat runtime replaced it. BUT asm fixtures intentionally keep a semihosting exit fallback (semihost_exit.inc) — that is NOT legacy, per CLAUDE.md.
- The shell driver was replaced by the C++ ./andesim driver as the only user-facing driver; tests/e2e.sh is still the harness used internally (NOT legacy).

Rules:
- ONLY tracked files (git ls-files). Ignore untracked/gitignored files entirely.
- include/ in andesim is a git submodule (shared ABI pinned by BOTH repos) — never propose deletions inside it. Same for vsim external/ submodules.
- Do not propose deleting anything just because it looks old — you need positive evidence it is dead: unreferenced (grep both repos), superseded, or describes removed behavior.
- Check references across BOTH repos before claiming dead (vsim scripts may call andesim files and vice versa).
- Use git log --follow on suspicious files to understand their story.
Return findings as structured data. Be precise with paths and line ranges.

Scope: andesim tests/ (e2e.sh, fixtures/, andes_sim/, plugin/, vplat/, hybrid/ if present). Find legacy: fixtures no ,longer wired into any runner (check tests/e2e.sh, scripts/run_e2e.sh, cmake in the vsim repo at /home/nick/work/vsim_andesim/cmake/), harness code for removed features (QEMU2 leg), Makefile targets building nothing used, dead helper functions. Remember semihost_exit.inc fallback in asm fixtures is intentional, not legacy.

2	# End-to-end harness: QEMU 1 + plugin -> vsim (2-phase, no QEMU2 handback).
3	#
4	# Memory between QEMU and vsim is shared via an /dev/shm-backed mmap
5	# (128 MB). Works for both asm fixtures (handoff_roundtrip, rt_*) and
6	# C-level fixtures (rt_c_*). C fixtures require shared mmap so the
7	# stack/heap survives handoffs; asm fixtures don't need it but run
8	# fine with it.
9	#
10	# Env:
11	#   FIXTURE         REQUIRED. .elf name under tests/fixtures/ (no .elf suffix).
12	#   TRIGGER_MODE    marker | pc (default marker).
13	#   ROI_START       pc mode switch-in PC: a 0x address or a symbol in
14	#                   $VSIM_ELF. If BOTH ROI_START and ROI_END are unset, they
15	#                   are auto-derived from the fixture's ROI marker HINTs via
16	#                   objdump (see roi_markers_from_disasm) -- the bulk runner
17	#                   relies on this; ./andesim run always passes them explicitly.
18	#   ROI_END         pc mode switch-out PC, same forms / same auto-derivation.
19	#   TIMEOUT         vsim leg timeout in seconds (default 60).
20	#   CHECK_MCYCLE_MONOTONIC=1   assert mcycle/minstret strictly increased
21	#                              between QEMU 1's drain and vsim's drain.
22	#   CHECK_PRIV=<0|1|3>         assert both drained state files carry this

24	#   CHECK_VSIM_STDOUT=<re>     assert the vsim leg's output (guest UART rides

26	#                              for fixtures that verify a result INSIDE the
27	#                              ROI and print a verdict (code after the exit
28	#                              marker never runs on the vsim leg).
29	#   ILM_SIZE / DLM_SIZE  LM content transport override, in bytes. Unset =
30	#                        probe $VSIM_BIN --describe (mirrors the driver's
31	#                        wiring); 0 = force that memory's transport OFF
32	#                        (negative-control knob).

121	# driver's run_plan wiring. The engine's --describe reports its memories in
122	# BYTES; when a size is > 0 the QEMU plugin drains that memory's content to
123	# a sidecar next to the state file and the vsim leg backdoor-loads it
124	# (--ilm/--dlm/--hvm). An engine without the memory (or an older binary
125	# whose --describe lacks the field) adds nothing. ILM_SIZE/DLM_SIZE/HVM_SIZE

127	# (negative-control knob).

130	# engine's describe -- the raw analog of the driver's
131	# --print-qemu-config/-readconfig sync), so a transport-off negative still
132	# runs the guest against the engine's real geometry. This matters twice:
133	# QEMU's compiled-in ILM default is 2 MB at 0x0, which SHADOWS the program
134	# image at 0x100000 the moment a guest sets milmb.EN (the engine's real
135	# 64 KB ends at 0xFFFF); and QEMU's HVM default is 1 BYTE

235	fi

237	# LM/HVM exit-dump check: vsim dumps its ILM/DLM/HVM content next to the
238	# handoff-out state file; for a ROI that never writes those memories, the

251	      cmp "$STATE_QEMU.$kind" "$STATE_VSIM.$kind" | head -3

253	    fi
254	  done

270	# Kernel cycles (always) + opt-in monotonic check. Offsets locked by
271	# state_abi_check.h (mcycle@624, minstret@632). vsim restores mcycle from
272	# QEMU 1's drain then counts real clock cycles, so vsim_mcycle - qemu1_mcycle
273	# is the measured region's cycle count. Runs before the RC gate so the
274	# verdict is independent of any downstream-phase failure.
275	read_u64_le() { od -A n -j "$1" -N 8 -t u8 "$2" | tr -d ' \n'; }

277	  Q1_MCYCLE=$(read_u64_le 624 "$STATE_QEMU")
278	  Q1_MINST=$(read_u64_le  632 "$STATE_QEMU")
279	  V_MCYCLE=$(read_u64_le  624 "$STATE_VSIM")
280	  V_MINST=$(read_u64_le   632 "$STATE_VSIM")
281	  echo "[$FIXTURE kernel_cycles] $((V_MCYCLE - Q1_MCYCLE))  (vsim mcycle=$V_MCYCLE - qemu1 mcycle=$Q1_MCYCLE)"
282	  # L6: privilege survives the handoff. priv@24 locked by state_abi_check.h.
283	  if [ -n "${CHECK_PRIV:-}" ]; then
284	    Q1_PRIV=$(read_u64_le 24 "$STATE_QEMU")
285	    V_PRIV=$(read_u64_le  24 "$STATE_VSIM")
286	    echo "[$FIXTURE priv] qemu1=$Q1_PRIV vsim=$V_PRIV expected=$CHECK_PRIV"
287	    if [ "$Q1_PRIV" != "$CHECK_PRIV" ] || [ "$V_PRIV" != "$CHECK_PRIV" ]; then
288	      echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: drained priv mismatch (expected $CHECK_PRIV)"
289	      exit 1
290	    fi
291	  fi
292	  if [ "${CHECK_MCYCLE_MONOTONIC:-0}" = "1" ]; then
293	    echo "[$FIXTURE mcycle/minstret] qemu1: mcycle=$Q1_MCYCLE minstret=$Q1_MINST"
294	    echo "[$FIXTURE mcycle/minstret] vsim:  mcycle=$V_MCYCLE minstret=$V_MINST"
295	    if [ "$V_MCYCLE" -le "$Q1_MCYCLE" ]; then
296	      echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: mcycle not strictly increasing across vsim"
297	      exit 1
298	    fi
299	    if [ "$V_MINST" -le "$Q1_MINST" ]; then
300	      echo "FAIL[$FIXTURE]: minstret not strictly increasing across vsim"
301	      exit 1
302	    fi
303	    echo "[$FIXTURE mcycle/minstret] PASS: strictly increasing"
304	  fi
305	fi
306	
307	echo "[$FIXTURE PASS] 2-phase handoff complete (QEMU 1 drain -> vsim drain)"

docs/register_transport_tutorial.ipynb:17:   "source": "## Q1. How do we decide whether to transport the floating-point and vector registers?

**Answer:** The QEMU plugin decides at drain time by *asking QEMU which registers it advertises*. If QEMU exposes the FP registers, we set `HYBRID_FLAG_FP` and carry them. If it exposes the vector registers with a sane `vlenb`, we set `HYBRID_FLAG_V` and carry them. It is capability detection, not a hand-set switch. **Both are supported today.**

### One idea behind both: a handle means "this CPU has it"

`resolve_handles()` looks up every register by name. `find_reg` returns a handle if QEMU advertised that register, else `NULL`:

```c
// qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c:121
static struct qemu_plugin_register *find_reg(GArray *regs, const char *name) {
    for (guint i = 0; i < regs->len; i++) {
        // ... if the name matches, return rd->handle;
    }
    return NULL;   // not advertised -> this CPU does not expose it
}
```

So "handle is non-NULL" is the plugin's proxy for "this CPU has this register." FP and V both build on this one check.

### Floating-point: any FP handle -> transport

```c
// hybrid_handoff.c:296
int has_fp = 0;
for (int i = 0; i < 32; i++) {
    s.fpr[i] = read_reg64(v->fpr[i]);
    if (v->fpr[i]) has_fp = 1;      // at least one f-register was advertised
}
if (has_fp) s.flags |= HYBRID_FLAG_FP;
s.fcsr = read_reg64(v->fcsr);        // fcsr rides the FP flag
```

Rule: **carry FP iff QEMU advertised the F/D extension** (it exposes `f0..f31`). `fcsr` travels with the same flag.

### Vector: a small policy, not just a bool

V has more failure modes than FP: V can be *disabled at runtime*, the stub can *half-advertise* V, or the hardware `VLEN` can be *wider than the wire format*. A pure decision function covers every case:

```c
// include/hybrid/v_drain_policy.h  (its own truth table)
//   no vlenb, no other V          -> SKIP    (no V at all)
//   no vlenb, but vtype/vl/...     -> ABORT   (partial advertisement -> refuse)
//   vlenb advertised, no other V   -> SKIP
//   vlenb, other V, vlenb == 0     -> SKIP    (V disabled at runtime)
//   vlenb, other V, vlenb > 128    -> ABORT   (L11: wire format cannot hold it)
//   otherwise                      -> OK
```

The plugin calls it and acts on the verdict:

```c
// hybrid_handoff.c:379
HybridVDrainPolicy vpol = hybrid_v_drain_policy(v->vlenb != NULL, has_other_v, s.vlenb);
if (vpol == HYBRID_V_DRAIN_ABORT) { /* print reason */ exit(2); }
if (vpol == HYBRID_V_DRAIN_OK) {
    s.flags |= HYBRID_FLAG_V;
    for (int i = 0; i < 32; i++)                    // copy vlenb bytes per v-register
        read_reg_bytes(v->vreg[i], &s.vreg[i * 128], s.vlenb);
}
```

Rule: **carry V iff QEMU advertised the V extension with a non-zero `vlenb` <= 128 bytes** (VLEN <= 1024). A partial or oversized advertisement is a hard error (`exit(2)`), never a silent skip -- silently skipping would make the resume side mis-restore.

### The consumer obeys the same flags

The flags are the single gate on the far side. `--verify` compares FP / V blocks only when the matching flag is set:

```cpp
// driver/state_diff.cpp:50
if (ref.flags & HYBRID_FLAG_FP) { /* compare f0..f31, fcsr */ }
if (ref.flags & HYBRID_FLAG_V)  { /* compare vstart/vtype/vl/vlenb/vxsat/vxrm/vcsr, v0..v31 */ }
```

`ResumeDriver` (vsim side) likewise restores each block only under its flag: `fcsr` under FP, and the full V restore order under V (see CLAUDE.md, "V-State Transport").

### Supported? Yes.

| Block | Decided by | Flag | Carried | Verified |
|-------|-----------|------|---------|----------|
| `f0..f31` + `fcsr` | any f-register handle advertised | `HYBRID_FLAG_FP` | yes | yes (`state_diff.cpp:50`) |
| `v0..v31` + V-CSRs | `hybrid_v_drain_policy() == OK` | `HYBRID_FLAG_V` | yes (via scratch page) | yes (`state_diff.cpp:56`) |

Fixtures that exercise them: `rt_all_fprs.S` (FP), `rt_c_v_regs` and `rt_c_v_csrs` (V).",
docs/andes_sim_limitations.ipynb:555:   "source": "## Tier 3 - Configuration and accuracy limits

### L10. Engines are pluggable now, but machine + scratch GPA stay fixed

- When it bites: any machine other than `andes_ae350`, any CPU outside the
  `andes-ax45mpv` family, or any RAM base other than 0.
- What happens: engines are now drop-in (`andesim list engines`,
  `--engine ID`, discovered via `--describe` or a `.json` sidecar), and the
  QEMU leg's `-cpu ...,vlen={vlen}` is filled from the chosen engine's
  descriptor (`driver/engine_registry.cpp:46`). But `-machine andes_ae350`
  and the `andes-ax45mpv` CPU name are still literals
  (`engine_registry.cpp:46,54`). The V-register scratch address is NO LONGER a
  fixed constant -- it is the mmap's top page (`v_scratch_gpa(ram_base,
  ram_size)`, L26), derived from the runtime RAM base + size, so it adapts to
  any base and is no longer a porting blocker.
- Where: `driver/engine_registry.cpp:46,54`.
- Status: PARTIALLY RELAXED: engine variant + VLEN are pluggable, and the
  scratch GPA is now runtime-derived (L26); the machine and the CPU family are
  still literals that block porting to another core.

### L11. [RESOLVED 2026-06-12: ceiling raised to VLEN 1024, over-limit aborts] VLEN ceiling  (F-T3.4)

- Was: the wire format reserved 64 bytes per vector register (VLEN 512)
  and the plugin CLAMPED the drained bytes to that with no warning - a
  wider engine silently lost the upper bytes of every V register. The
  standalone fast model also hardcoded `vlen=512`.
- Now (supported range: VLEN 128..1024):
  - `HYBRID_VLEN_BYTES_MAX = 128` (`state_abi.h`), state version 2;
    every reader (driver `state.hpp`, vsim `state_loader.hpp`) rejects version-1 files loudly.
  - The plugin REFUSES to drain an over-ceiling vlenb
    (`hybrid_v_drain_policy`, `include/hybrid/v_drain_policy.h`) instead
    of clamping; vsim's `load_state` rejects an over-ceiling state file
    the same way.
  - Inside `andesim run` the legs still cannot disagree (descriptor
    sync, unchanged). A standalone fast run overrides the built-in
    `vlen=512` via the passthrough tail:
    `andesim run --mode fast app.elf -- -cpu andes-ax45mpv,vlen=1024`
    (the last `-cpu` wins).
- Tests: `tests/hybrid/e2e_vlen1024_drain.sh` (QEMU leg at vlen=1024
  drains vlenb=128 with the full 128-byte register intact + the fast
  standalone override); fixture `tests/fixtures/rt_c_v_fill.c`
  (whole-register fill, in-ROI self-check; runs in the marker/pc
  suites); unit cases in `state_abi.test.cpp`, `v_drain_policy.test.cpp`,
  `state_loader.test.cpp`.
- Verified per VLEN (2026-06-12). Drain checks: drained `vlenb` ==
  VLEN/8, the LAST live byte of v8 carries the fill pattern (truncation
  would zero it), and the byte just past the live span is 0:

| VLEN | plugin drain (QEMU leg) | fast standalone | hybrid round-trip on RTL    |
|------|-------------------------|-----------------|------------------------------|
| 128  | pass (vlenb=16)         | pass            | pass (`vsim:ax66_makatau`)   |
| 256  | pass (vlenb=32)         | pass            | no RTL config built          |
| 512  | pass (vlenb=64)         | pass            | pass (e2e 39/39 + `--verify` on `vsim:ax45mpv_premium`) |
| 1024 | pass (vlenb=128)        | pass            | no RTL config built          |

- Residual (tracked as ROADMAP F-ENG-03): hand-driven legs at two
  DIFFERENT under-ceiling VLENs are caught only by the fixture
  self-check; a vsim-side compare of the live hart vlenb against
  `state.vlenb` at resume is still open. No built RTL engine reports
  VLEN 256 or 1024 today (`ax46mpv_advanced`'s cfg sets `NDS_VLEN 1024`
  but its built binary describes `vlen=512`), so those two widths are
  validated on the QEMU side; the vsim transport is vlenb-driven by
  construction. With a real VLEN-1024 RTL build, `rt_c_v_fill` through
  `--mode hybrid --verify` is the ready-made acceptance test.
- Status: RESOLVED (2026-06-12) for the supported range 128..1024.

### L12. [RESOLVED: the CSR-write trigger was replaced by marker HINTs] CSR 0x7C0 collision

- The old default trigger matched `csrwi 0x7C0, 0/1`, so a real write to
  that CSR would false-trigger a handoff. The default trigger is now the
  marker HINT pair `slti x0, x0, 0x5A0/0x5A1` - rd=x0 makes them
  architectural NOPs, no CSR is repurposed, and a compiler never emits them
  on its own (users get them from `<andesim/ROI.h>`). Binaries you cannot
  edit use `--trigger pc` instead.
- Where: `qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c:799-810` (marker registration; the
  `slti` HINTs are matched in `include/hybrid/insn_match.h:32-33`);
  `src/hybrid/csr_trigger.hpp` (now matches the same HINTs).
- Status: RESOLVED by the trigger redesign.

### L13. [RESOLVED: exact by construction for SLTI] marker must be a 32-bit instruction  (B18)

- The matcher still skips any instruction whose size is not 4 bytes, but
  the markers are now `slti x0, x0, imm` and SLTI has no compressed form,
  so the `sz != 4` skip is exact rather than an approximation
  (`hybrid_handoff.c:800-805`, comment says exactly this).
- Status: RESOLVED (was a documented caveat of the old CSR marker).

### L21. Andes vendor CSRs are only partially transported  (new 2026-05-28; cache/misc pair landed 2026-06-16)

- When it bites: any workload whose behavior or cycle figure depends on
  Andes-specific CSRs OTHER than the cache / misc pair (`mmsc_cfg,
  micm_cfg, mdcm_cfg, mxstatus, mdcause, mnvec, mslideleg`, ...).
- What happens: the cache machine-setup pair `mcache_ctl` (0x7CA) and
  `mmisc_ctl` (0x7D0) now round-trips. crt0 enables the L1 I/D caches via
  `csrw mcache_ctl`, but that write runs on the cache-less functional
  engine; without carrying it the cycle engine resumed at the ROI with
  caches at their reset default -- DISABLED -- so the whole window ran
  uncached and the figure was inflated severalfold (hello `main`->`_exit`:
  14707 -> 2871 cycles). All OTHER Andes vendor CSRs still do not appear
  in `hybrid_state_v1`; vsim runs the ROI with whatever its reset /
  boot-time values were, so remaining prefetcher / branch-predictor / ECC
  controls can still shape the cycle count -- an accuracy hazard for those.
- Where: `include/hybrid/state_abi.h` (mcache_ctl/mmisc_ctl fields, rest
  absent); `qemu_plugin/hybrid_handoff.c` (drains the pair by gdbstub
  name); `resume_driver.hpp` (tolerant restore, `kCsrMcacheCtl` /
  `kCsrMmiscCtl`).
- Status: PARTIAL. The cycle-shaping cache pair is transported (the L20
  fix recipe: one `uint64` each carved from `reserved[]`, drained by name,
  restored via abstract-or-PB, no version bump). The remaining vendor CSRs
  await a v2 Andes block labelling each as microarch-only (read-only /
  boot-set) or software-visible (must round-trip).

### L26. [RESOLVED 2026-06-16] V transport scratch moved above the program's RAM  (new 2026-06-15)

- **Was**: the V-register transport staged 32 vector registers through a fixed
  guest address `kVScratchGpa = 0x00FF0000` (15 MiB), INSIDE the program's RAM.
  On every resume on a V-capable core -- the V flag is set from register
  ADVERTISEMENT, not use, so even a program that issues no V instruction
  triggers it -- `ResumeDriver` wrote the drained V bytes there, silently
  clobbering any program data at that address. Repro: `break_vscratch.S`.
- **Why a scratch page is needed at all**: the RISC-V Debug Module has no
  abstract command for `v0..v31`, so vsim moves them by executing `vle8.v` /
  `vse8.v` in the Program Buffer against a known guest-RAM staging page
  (`v_regfile_xfer.hpp`, `program_buffer.hpp`).
- **Fix (scheme D; F1+F2+F3)**:
  1. The scratch is no longer a constant -- it is the TOP page of the mapped
     RAM span, `v_scratch_gpa(ram_base, ram_size) = ram_base + ram_size -
     HYBRID_V_SCRATCH_BYTES`. ResumeDriver/StateDrain take it as a required-
     when-V argument; a V handoff with it unset throws (no silent transport
     through a bogus address).
  2. The driver maps ONE PAGE MORE than `--mem-size` (`shm.cpp`
     `physical_mmap_bytes`), so the scratch sits at `ram_base + --mem-size` --
     just ABOVE the program's declared RAM. No program layout (low stack,
     top-of-RAM stack, or a heap grown to the ceiling) can reach a page past its
     own RAM, so the scratch can never be clobbered. `--mem-size` is capped at
     2 GiB minus the page.
  3. A load-time guard (`elf_load_top` + `cmd_run.cpp`) rejects an ELF whose
     static image extends into the reserved page (linked for more RAM than
     `--mem-size` grants) with a clear "raise --mem-size" message, instead of
     silent corruption.
- **Effect on users**: none visible -- you get your full `--mem-size`; the
  reservation is one hidden page the simulator adds on top, and no address
  within your declared RAM is off-limits.
- **Tests**: `v_regfile_xfer` / `resume_driver` / `state_drain` unit suites
  (top-page GPA + unset guard); `infra-test` (physical size + cap); `elf-syms`
  (load-top + reject). `break_vscratch.S` now PASSES (0x00FF0000 is no longer
  used); new `break_vscratch_top.S` PASSES (a sentinel at the program's LAST
  page survives the transport, proving the scratch sits above program RAM);
  full marker e2e 22/22 + V e2e 4/4.
- **Status**: RESOLVED (2026-06-16)."

1	#!/usr/bin/env bash
2	# hotloops.sh LLM report contract: each loop block carries a ready hybrid
3	# pc window, `measure: --pc-start 0x<entry> --pc-end 0x<ret>`, derived from
4	# the loop's enclosing function. The loop's own pc_range is NOT a usable
5	# window (one-shot pc triggers fire on the first hit, so header..tail
6	# measures a single iteration); the function span covers every iteration
7	# and needs no objdump step from the user.
8	#
9	# Builds a tiny single-ret RVV kernel (vplat runtime), runs the detector,
10	# and checks the measure line against the toolchain's own nm/objdump as
11	# the oracle.
12	
13	set -uo pipefail
14	
15	SCRIPT_DIR=$(cd -- "$(dirname -- "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")" && pwd)
16	ROOT=$(cd -- "$SCRIPT_DIR/../.." && pwd)
17	
18	QEMU_BIN="${VSIM_QEMU:-$ROOT/build/qemu/qemu-system-riscv64}"
19	PLUGIN="$ROOT/build/qemu/contrib/plugins/libhotloops.so"
20	
21	. "$ROOT/config.env" 2>/dev/null || true
22	GCC="${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:-}/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-gcc"
23	NM="${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:-}/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-nm"
24	OBJDUMP="${HYBRID_TOOLCHAIN:-}/bin/riscv64-unknown-elf-objdump"
25	
26	[ -x "$QEMU_BIN" ] || { echo "SKIP: qemu not built"; exit 0; }
27	[ -f "$PLUGIN" ] || { echo "SKIP: hotloops plugin not built"; exit 0; }
28	[ -x "$GCC" ] || { echo "SKIP: no riscv toolchain"; exit 0; }
29	[ -d "$ROOT/build/runtime" ] || { echo "SKIP: vplat runtime not built"; exit 0; }
30	
31	TMP=$(mktemp -d -t hotloops-measure.XXXXXX)
32	trap 'rm -rf "$TMP"' EXIT
33	
34	cat > "$TMP/vadd.c" <<'EOF'
35	#include <stdint.h>
36	#include <riscv_vector.h>
37	static int32_t a[64], b[64];
38	__attribute__((noinline)) static void vadd_kernel(void)
39	{
40	  for (int r = 0; r < 50; r++)
41	    for (int i = 0; i < 64;) {
42	      size_t vl = __riscv_vsetvl_e32m1((size_t) (64 - i));
43	      vint32m1_t va = __riscv_vle32_v_i32m1(&a[i], vl);
44	      vint32m1_t vb = __riscv_vle32_v_i32m1(&b[i], vl);
45	      __riscv_vse32_v_i32m1(&a[i], __riscv_vadd_vv_i32m1(va, vb, vl), vl);
46	      i += (int) vl;
47	    }
48	}
49	int main(void) { vadd_kernel(); return 0; }
50	EOF
51	
52	"$GCC" -march=rv64gcv -mabi=lp64d -O1 \
53	  -B "$ROOT/build/runtime" -specs=andesim.specs \
54	  "$TMP/vadd.c" -o "$TMP/vadd.elf" \
55	  || { echo "FAIL[hotloops_measure]: fixture build failed"; exit 1; }
56	
57	REPORT=$("$ROOT/QEMU/scripts/hotloops.sh" \
58	           --qemu "$QEMU_BIN" --plugin "$PLUGIN" \
59	           --cpu "andes-ax45mpv,vext_spec=v1.0,vlen=512" \
60	           --min-iters 10 "$TMP/vadd.elf" 2>/dev/null)
61	
62	echo "$REPORT" | grep -q "L1 \[hottest\]" \
63	  || { echo "FAIL[hotloops_measure]: no hottest loop reported"; echo "$REPORT"; exit 1; }
64	
65	MEASURE=$(echo "$REPORT" | grep -m1 "^measure:")
66	[ -n "$MEASURE" ] \
67	  || { echo "FAIL[hotloops_measure]: no measure: line in the report"; echo "$REPORT"; exit 1; }
68	
69	GOT_S=$(echo "$MEASURE" | grep -o -- "--pc-start 0x[0-9a-f]*" | awk '{print $2}')
70	GOT_E=$(echo "$MEASURE" | grep -o -- "--pc-end 0x[0-9a-f]*" | awk '{print $2}')
71	
72	# Oracle: the kernel's entry from nm; its return = the function's last
73	# instruction (single-epilogue at -O1; objdump flavors disagree on the
74	# `ret` vs `c.jr ra` spelling, so match by position, not mnemonic).
75	WANT_S=$(printf '0x%x' "0x$("$NM" "$TMP/vadd.elf" | awk '$3=="vadd_kernel"{print $1; exit}')")
76	WANT_E=$(printf '0x%x' "0x$("$OBJDUMP" -d "$TMP/vadd.elf" \
77	  | sed -n '/<vadd_kernel>:/,/^$/p' | grep -E '^[ ]+[0-9a-f]+:' \
78	  | tail -1 | awk '{sub(":","",$1); print $1}')")
79	
80	if [ "$GOT_S" != "$WANT_S" ] || [ "$GOT_E" != "$WANT_E" ]; then
81	  echo "FAIL[hotloops_measure]: window $GOT_S..$GOT_E, want $WANT_S..$WANT_E"
82	  echo "$MEASURE"
83	  exit 1
84	fi
85	
86	echo "$REPORT" | grep -q "Measure all of" \
87	  || { echo "FAIL[hotloops_measure]: TL;DR carries no measure hint"; exit 1; }
88	
89	# measure_loop: the loop's own first-pass window, [header, fall-through of
90	# the backward branch). pc-start = pc_range start; pc-end = the insn AFTER
91	# the branch in the disassembly (exact, works for compressed branches too).
92	ML=$(echo "$REPORT" | grep -m1 "^measure_loop:")
93	[ -n "$ML" ] \
94	  || { echo "FAIL[hotloops_measure]: no measure_loop: line"; echo "$REPORT"; exit 1; }
95	ML_S=$(echo "$ML" | grep -o -- "--pc-start 0x[0-9a-f]*" | awk '{print $2}')
96	ML_E=$(echo "$ML" | grep -o -- "--pc-end 0x[0-9a-f]*" | awk '{print $2}')
97	
98	RANGE=$(echo "$REPORT" | grep -m1 "^pc_range:")
99	R_S=$(echo "$RANGE" | awk '{print $2}')
100	R_E=$(echo "$RANGE" | awk '{print $4}')
101	WANT_FT=$(printf '0x%x' "0x$("$OBJDUMP" -d "$TMP/vadd.elf" \
102	  | awk -v tail="${R_E#0x}" 'f{sub(":","",$1); print $1; exit}
103	                             $1 == tail":"{f=1}')")
104	
105	if [ "$ML_S" != "$R_S" ] || [ "$ML_E" != "$WANT_FT" ]; then
106	  echo "FAIL[hotloops_measure]: measure_loop $ML_S..$ML_E, want $R_S..$WANT_FT"
107	  echo "$ML"
108	  exit 1
109	fi
110	
111	echo "PASS[hotloops_measure]: measure = $GOT_S .. $GOT_E (function), measure_loop = $ML_S .. $ML_E (first pass)"
112

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Hot inner-loop detector wrapper (system-mode, baremetal RISC-V).
#
# Runs a baremetal ELF under qemu-system-<arch> with the hotloops plugin
# and prints a sorted table of detected backward branches:
#
#   iters | start_pc -> end_pc | function:offset
#
# Usage:
#   scripts/hotloops.sh [opts] <elf>
#
# Options:
#   --arch <riscv32|riscv64|auto>   Target arch (default: auto)
#   --qemu <path>                   Override qemu-system binary
#   --plugin <path>                 Override plugin .so
#   --machine <name>                -M <name> (default andes_ae350)
#   --cpu <spec>                    -cpu <spec>
#                                   (default andes-ax45mpv,vext_spec=v1.0,vlen=1024)
#   --qemu-config <file>            -readconfig <file> (e.g. AE350 device cfg)
#   --cwd <dir>                     chdir before launching QEMU so semihosting
#                                   opens (fread of bin/*.bin) resolve
#   --qemu-arg <arg>                Append an extra arg to the QEMU command
#                                   (repeatable)
#   --limit <N>                     Top-N loops to print (default 50)
#   --min-iters <N>                 Drop loops with fewer than N iters (default 1)
#   --objdump <path>                Override objdump (resolves symbols)
#   --addr2line <path>              Override addr2line (resolves source lines)
#   --no-source                     Disable source file:line resolution
#   --raw                           Print raw plugin output, no formatting
#   --optimize-rvv                  Only report loops with at least one RVV
#                                   instruction (default: on)
#   --no-optimize-rvv               Disable the RVV-only filter
#   --llm                           Emit a Markdown report tuned for LLM
#                                   consumption: TL;DR + per-loop fact-sheets
#                                   with stable IDs, source snippets, RVV
#                                   instruction listings, nesting, and direct
#                                   callees (default: on).
#   --no-llm                        Emit the plain human-readable table.
